I find the statement "now with vitamins" very strange and questionable on multiple levels. 

First, if this were a quality dairy product, it would already be packed with vitamins. Muller boasting this "now" has vitamins tells me it's an ultra-ultra-processed product, so much so that they felt they couldn't say it has vitamins unless they dumped synthetic versions in as additives.

Second, it really speaks to the demographic they're going for, i.e. people who have zero idea what a healthy diet actually looks like, and might actually think they're being "healthy" eating this ultra-processed product. Sorry, but healthy eating isn't a case of ticking a box and you're good. The opposite is closer to the truth, i.e. controlling your calories throughout the entire week and favouring natural whole foods that are legitimately nutritionally rich, over ultra-processed junk.

Sorry for the rant, but this advert is littered with marketing nonsense and actually misleads the public as to what healthy eating is, and that needs to be called out.
